title: WS9 row S07 (interrupt child) vs our llm-proxy — v2 multi-agent interrupt (RT-M11 lineage, interrupt_agent tool): ACP parent qwen3.8-27b (responses wire) spawns a same-model child worker (qwen3.8-27b — same wire+boundary, isolating the interrupt semantics from cross-wire projection) with a LONG five-stage task; the parent then calls interrupt_agent on the running child; the child must be REUSABLE after interruption (followup_task -> the child delivers WS9-S07-AFTER over the mailbox). The v2 arm is LIVE in the hermetic config (features.multi_agent_v2=true + row-level, live config at recon — no in-case arm patch; re-verify wire-intact at Phase-B launch per WAVE-S PG-3). Verdict semantics: PASS = the session survives the child interrupt end-to-end — no error terminal, the parent acknowledges (INTERRUPTED), and the interrupted child completed the follow-up (WS9-S07-AFTER in the parent's final text: the interrupt left the child reusable with its task identity intact — the interrupt_agent contract: 'interrupts the current turn without deleting history or task identity'). The tool-flow engaged pin (escaped-arguments marker) is a premise control: 0-hit => VACUOUS (the model never issued the spawn/interrupt tool calls — temperament, recorded). FAIL (S3 report-and-stop) = an unrecovered error terminal, a hung wait (watchdog), or a child that cannot be re-tasked after interruption (the AFTER report never arrives AND the tool flow was observed — the interrupt deleted the task identity). The exact interrupt call shape (task_name vs id targeting) is the recorded evidence for review (recon), not a scored pin — the model may target the task by name or id. No PROP gate (interrupt_agent is in-tree, v2 tool set).

steps.prompt: Use the spawn_agent tool to start a background agent named worker with model qwen3.8-27b. Give it this task: write a long essay about the history of lighthouses in five stages; after each stage use the send_message tool to report the stage number to the parent agent (root), and keep going until all five stages are reported; do not finish before all five stages are sent.
The worker is running. Interrupt its current turn now: call the interrupt_agent tool targeting worker. Then reply with exactly: INTERRUPTED

Now reuse the interrupted worker: use the followup_task tool to send worker the follow-up task: use the send_message tool to send the parent agent (root) a message containing exactly: WS9-S07-AFTER, and only then finish. Wait with wait_agent, then reply with exactly: WS9-S07-AFTER PARENT-OK

ndjson.label: INTERRUPT ACKNOWLEDGED: the parent completed the interrupt turn (the interrupt_agent call did not error-terminate the session).

CHILD REUSABLE AFTER INTERRUPT: the interrupted worker completed the follow-up and delivered WS9-S07-AFTER over the mailbox — the interrupt left the task identity and history intact (the interrupt_agent contract).

wire.label: CONTROL (anti-vacuous pin): an escaped tool-arguments line (the form ONLY tool calls carry — prompt text and the tools[] schema cannot false-satisfy it) marks the v2 flow (spawn_agent/interrupt_agent/followup_task against task_name worker) on the parent's wire. 0-hit = the model never issued the tool calls (VACUOUS, temperament).

NO RETRY STORM: 3 parent requests (spawn/interrupt/reuse turns) + child stage requests (<=5 stage reports) + side calls fit 4-9; <3 = the flow never ran (cross-check the control pin); >9 = retry storm around the interrupt = defect (S3).

INTERRUPT EVIDENCE RECORD: records every captured line carrying the escaped task_name worker tool-arguments (spawn vs interrupt vs followup calls — the exact interrupt targeting shape, name vs id, is read here on review). recon — always records, never fails.
VERDICT RECORD: merged ndjson final text head (the post-reuse terminal output, verbatim). recon — always records, never fails.
